Teaching a small model to drive Nushell

LFM3 1.7B turns a plain request into one run_nushell tool call. A call counts only if running it returns the reference value.
  • Before training: 8% of 40 held-out requests.
  • After training: 95% of the same 40, and 92.6% of all 231.
  • Other models: gpt-6-luna 32.5% of 40, claude-haiku-5-5 17.5% of 40.
  • Training: one LoRA of rank 8 on all linear layers (8.2 M parameters), 825 rows × 2 epochs, 414 updates, on a Mac with MLX.
  • In this notebook: the generated environments, the command chains and requests, the training run, the model in 3D with and without its LoRA, and the comparison with other models.

Data gen & rephrase

List what is in tools; then return their names; then count the lines mentioning 'scheduler' in each file and rank the files with any, most hits first, as file and hits; then keep the last 1; then count them. 
let found = (ls tools | get name); $found | where ($it | path type) == file | par-each {|f| {file: $f, hits: (open --raw $f | lines | where ($it | str contains -i 'scheduler') | length)} } | where hits > 0 | sort-by file | sort-by hits --reverse | last 1 | length
